description: Deterministic, source-addressed candidate dispositions. Overlapping source entries remain distinct.

disposition.reason: ATTACKER_DEPLOYED: the address the PoC targets was deployed by the attacker (0xd3641c912a6a4c30338787e3c464420b561a9467), so it is attack infrastructure, not the protocol's code. The real Arcadia victim contract was never pinned; the incident can re-enter with a verified victim.

LOSS_NOT_ESTABLISHED: the selected transaction exploits transferProxy's unchecked _value + _feeSmt addition and creates artificial SMT ledger balances, but its receipt and call trace transfer no ETH or external reserve asset. Subsequent onchain activity only sends the artificial SMT to exchange deposit addresses; the attacker address records no onchain sale proceeds. The inherited $140M figure has no asset-flow or valuation provenance and does not establish at least $1,000 of stolen or permanently locked assets.

candidate.name: Wanchain Cardano bridge signature verification flaw

disposition.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: DefiLlama records the incident on Cardano only, 10m USD, classification 'Input Validation', technique 'Signature Verification Flaw', bridgeHack true, targetType 'Chain', and names the defective code's language as Haskell. Wanchain's Cardano-side bridge logic is a Plutus validator written in Plutus Tx / Haskell and addressed by a Cardano script address, so there is neither an eip155 address nor EVM runtime bytecode whose age this dataset could measure, and the depleted vault is on Cardano rather than on the BNB Chain leg the web lead names. The cohort is eip155-only. Re-enter only if a postmortem shows the released value actually came out of a Wanchain contract deployed on BNB Chain or another eip155 chain, which would move the victim onto an EVM chain.

NON_EVM_CHAIN and OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: DefiLlama records MyAlgo on Algorand, 9.2m USD, classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'CDN Compromise', targetType 'Wallet', language JavaScript. Algorand is not an eip155 chain, and the defective artefact was the wallet's browser JavaScript, served from a compromised CDN, which exfiltrated users' mnemonics; the subsequent transfers were valid Algorand payments signed with the stolen seeds. Both grounds bite independently: there is no EVM chain involved and no deployed contract executed any defective code, only client-side script outside any chain's state.

KEY_COMPROMISE: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Private Key Compromised', targetType 'AI Agent', 9.09m USD on Ethereum; the web lead agrees the compromised party was a third-party managed account rather than Astra Nova's own contracts. I checked the project's RVV token 0x80563fc2dd549bf36f82d3bf3b970bb5b08dbddb on BSC across blocks 65108334-65223513 (2025-10-19 to 2025-10-20): zero mints from the zero address and no single transfer at or above 10,000,000 RVV, so the token contract neither over-issued nor was drained and is not the victim. The loss is stolen-key movement of balances held in an externally owned or custodially managed account, with no deployed contract executing outside its specification and nothing whose code age could be measured.

INSIDER_RUG and ATTACKER_DEPLOYED: the Mantle mint did not use the lzReceive weakness at all, it used a hardcoded address literal planted in Holographs own operator bytecode. getJobDetails at block 65068617 shows the job was planted at block 63225816 on 2024-05-01, 43 days earlier, by 0x92d1f6fe..3d79: attacker EOA 0xc0ffee78121f208475abdd2cf0853a7afed64749 called adminCall(address,bytes) on 0x777c19834a1a2ff6353a1e9cfb7c799ed7943a11 which called operator.crossChainMessage. Four such plants exist. The operator implementation active then, 0x34b2521f33f224bf21b7f5a8e17354e90c59d453 (byte-identical on Mantle and Ethereum, runtime hash 0xa7a3b24b..1d5c), contains verbatim: require(msg.sender == address(_messagingModule()) || msg.sender == 0x777c19834a1a2ff6353a1e9cfb7c799ed7943a11), and _messagingModuleSlot held the canonical 0x7969414a..0271 throughout, so only the literal branch let the call through. 0x777c1983.. was created by 0xc0ffee78 through the attackers own CREATE2 factory 0x0c8af56f76.. on 2023-08-04, five months before the backdoored implementation existed; its getAdmin() is 0xc0ffee78 and its implementation slot points to unverified custom bytecode differing per chain, unlike Holographs canonical verified LayerZeroModule 0x7d4807de... Triggering it requires being that address, whose only entry is admin-gated adminCall, so the settled backdoor convention makes this author-or-attacker-installed authority rather than a defect any caller could trigger. The Ethereum leg 0x0cc143cc..46396 is downstream and yields nothing: its job hash 0x3f9c5cc1..6571 matches the last Mantle bridge-out 0x845dafda..6449 exactly, so Ethereum minted the legitimate counterpart of a real Mantle burn. All 10e9 HLG minted on Mantle was burned out in seven transactions and no other Mantle HLG mint exists in the tokens history. The lzReceive weakness described in reporting is real as code, only caller() == _lZEndpointSlot and _srcAddress[0:20] == address() are enforced, but no leg of this campaign on chains 1 or 5000 used it.

NON_EVM_CHAIN: Crema Finance is a concentrated-liquidity AMM deployed as a Solana BPF program written in Rust, and the whole campaign (flash loan from Solend, a self-created account passed where the pool's real tick account was expected, forged fee data, then claim) executed inside that Solana program. DefiLlama's hack registry records chain 'Solana', language 'Rust', classification 'Access Control', technique 'Improper Access Control', 8,800,000 USD, dated 2022-07-02. Solana has no eip155 chain id, emits no EVM bytecode and has no address whose runtime code could be hashed or aged, so cohort condition 1 (a defect in executed EVM code) cannot be satisfied. No Ethereum-side or other eip155 leg of this incident exists.

NON_EVM_CHAIN: ALEX is a DEX/launchpad on Stacks and its contracts are written in Clarity, not Solidity, running on the Stacks (Clarity VM) chain. DefiLlama records chain 'Stacks', language 'Clarity', classification 'Access Control', technique 'Caller Impersonation', 8,373,000 USD, dated 2025-06-06; the self-listing path failed to verify that the caller matched the token being listed. Stacks is not an eip155 chain, has no EVM runtime and no code hash that the verifier could pin, so the incident yields no code-age observation for this dataset. ALEX's earlier 2024-05-16 loss (4.3m, phishing) is likewise out of scope.

candidate.name: Haven Protocol xUSD offshore mint-validation flaws

disposition.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: Haven Protocol is a standalone CryptoNote/Monero fork with its own C++ daemon and ring-signature ledger; the 2021 exploit series minted unbacked xUSD/xAsset supply by abusing the offshore conversion and mint-validation logic in that daemon. DefiLlama records chain 'Haven', classification 'Token & Share Accounting', technique 'Infinite Mint', 8,187,000 USD, dated 2021-07-03, with language null (no Solidity involved). There is no eip155 chain, no contract address and no EVM transaction anywhere in the causal path, so cohort conditions 1 and 2 both fail.

OFFCHAIN_INFRASTRUCTURE: the Slope mobile wallet transmitted users' mnemonic seed phrases in clear text to Slope's centralised Sentry logging service, and whoever obtained that log signed ordinary transfers out of roughly nine thousand Solana accounts. DefiLlama records chain 'Solana', classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'Key Stored Publicly', targetType 'Wallet', 4,100,000 USD, dated 2022-08-02 (the web lead's ~8m is the upper press estimate). The defect is in an off-chain mobile client, the victims are externally owned Solana accounts, and Solana is not an eip155 chain: no deployed EVM code failed an invariant and there is no victim contract to age.

OFFCHAIN_INFRASTRUCTURE: attackers repackaged BitKeep's Android wallet (v7.2.9) with code that exfiltrated users' private keys and distributed it through unofficial download mirrors; the resulting drains are ordinary ERC-20/BEP-20 transfer and native-value transactions signed out of the victims' own externally owned accounts on BNB Chain, Ethereum, Polygon and Tron. The compromised artefact is a Java/Kotlin APK, not deployed EVM bytecode, and no contract in the causal path failed any invariant - the token contracts executed correctly for a caller holding the keys. There is therefore no victim contract and no defect-bearing code state to age. Compromised credentials and off-chain client behaviour are both excluded by METHODOLOGY.

candidate.name: Bittensor malicious PyPI package coldkey exfiltration

disposition.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: a malicious release of the `bittensor` Python package on PyPI exfiltrated users' unencrypted coldkeys, and the attacker then signed ordinary balance transfers on the Bittensor (Subtensor) Substrate chain. DefiLlama records language 'Python', classification 'Social Engineering', technique 'Malware', 8,000,000 USD, dated 2024-07-02, with an empty chain list. Bittensor is an SS58 Substrate network with no eip155 chain id and no EVM contract state at the time of the incident, and the defect lives in an off-chain Python dependency. Both cohort condition 1 (executed EVM code) and condition 2 (an eip155 anchor) fail.

CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION: the constructor stored iUSDC where the yUSDT strategy required iUSDT, the value persisted through the exploit, and the trace followed that address. Constructor-set persistent state can establish the vulnerable combination even when the runtime consumes it as written. Reopened pending a deployment anchor, artifact history, and structured loss review.

candidate.name: Trust Wallet browser extension 2.68 malicious release

disposition.reason: OFFCHAIN_INFRASTRUCTURE: the loss originates in a poisoned build of the Trust Wallet browser extension (version 2.68), i.e. in JavaScript shipped to users' browsers, not in any deployed contract. DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'Supply Chain Attack', targetType 'Wallet', chains 'Ethereum, Bitcoin, Solana', language null, 8,500,000 USD, dated 2025-12-25. The drains are ordinary transfers and approvals signed with keys the extension handed to the attacker, spread across chains two of which (Bitcoin, Solana) are not eip155 at all; the ERC-20 contracts touched on the Ethereum leg behaved exactly as written. No deployed EVM code violated an invariant, so there is no victim contract and no code age to measure.

candidate.name: Zapper frontend DNS hijack and drainer approvals

disposition.reason: OFFCHAIN_INFRASTRUCTURE: Zapper's domain was hijacked at the DNS layer and visitors were served a wallet-drainer page that asked them to sign ordinary ERC-20 approvals and Permit2 signatures; the subsequent transferFrom calls executed exactly as the token contracts specify. DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'DNS Hijack', chains 'Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Base', dated 2025-04-01, and notably records amount null - the 7.9m figure in the lead is an unsourced press estimate with no per-victim accounting. The victims are individual externally owned accounts, Zapper's own deployed contracts were not implicated, and no EVM code failed an invariant, so the incident yields neither a victim contract nor a measurable code state.

NON_EVM_CHAIN: ODIN.FUN is a token launchpad running as an Internet Computer canister written in Motoko; the attacker manipulated the bonding-curve spot price inside that canister to extract roughly 7m USD of BTC-denominated liquidity. DefiLlama records chain 'ICP', language 'Motoko', classification 'Oracle Manipulation', technique 'Spot Price Manipulation', 7,000,000 USD, dated 2025-08-12. The Internet Computer executes WebAssembly canisters, has no eip155 chain id, no EVM bytecode and no address whose runtime hash could be pinned, so no code-age observation is possible.

KEY_COMPROMISE: the attacker obtained a Yala deployment key and used the mint authority it carried to issue unbacked YU, then swapped the proceeds into roughly 7.64m USDC. DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Deployer Key Compromised', targetType 'Token', language 'Rust', chains 'Solana, Ethereum', 7,640,000 USD, dated 2025-09-14. The mint executed through the authority the deployed program grants its own key holder, so no invariant of any deployed code was violated; the primary leg is a Solana (Rust) program outside eip155, and the Ethereum leg is ordinary token movement. Compromised credentials and privileged actions are excluded by METHODOLOGY, so this yields no code-age row.

KEY_COMPROMISE: roughly 5,000 ETH (about 8m USD) left an HTX custodial hot wallet on 2023-09-24/25 as ordinary value transfers; HTX operates no deployed protocol contract that could have been exploited, and the attacker returned the funds on 2023-10-07 in exchange for a 250 ETH bounty that Justin Sun publicly confirmed - behaviour consistent with key theft, not with an exploited contract. DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Hot Wallet Key Compromised', targetType 'CEX', chain 'Ethereum', 8,000,000 USD, dated 2023-09-25. This is a distinct event from the 2023-11-22 HTX and HECO Bridge operator-key compromise already excluded in this file. With only externally owned custodial accounts in the causal path there is no victim contract, no exploit transaction against deployed code and no code state whose age could be measured.

KEY_COMPROMISE: Zoth's deployer key held the UUPS upgrade authority on the USD0PPSubVaultUpgradeable proxy 0x82f3a0392f58c50fa90542519832471bae93e43e, and whoever obtained it called upgradeToAndCall() in transaction 0xb2335f7bf58abbcaa006d0a2bed7db2c64a5dabed56fb1759260adc012c49abe at block 22094140 to install a self-authored implementation 0xc89d7894341e13d5067d003af5346b257d861f56 carrying an unrestricted withdraw(), then emptied the vault 36 seconds later in 0x33bf669d125d11c432ac9b52b9d56161101c072fd8b0ac2aa390f5760fb50ca4. The proxy was created by Zoth deployer 0x3604582f56565d7060d73829ffb9ebd579218dca, not by the attack sender 0x3b33c5cd948be5863b72cb3d6e9c0b36e67d01e5, and this was the seventh Upgraded event on the proxy. No pre-existing Zoth code failed an invariant: the upgrade mechanism executed exactly as designed for the holder of the upgrade key, and the only 'defective' artifact is the attacker's own implementation, whose 36-second mechanical age measures the attacker's deployment rather than any battle-tested code. DefiLlama also classifies it 'Key Compromise / Private Key Compromised'. This matches seed row protocols/zoth.json#0, which was already held out of the primary dataset for the same reason.

candidate.name: THORChain Asgard vault GG20 threshold-signature key reconstruction

disposition.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: THORChain's published post-mortem attributes the 2026-05-15 loss of about 10.7m USD across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Base and BNB Chain to a vulnerability in the GG20 threshold-ECDSA implementation used by THORNode: a malicious node operator progressively leaked key material until it could reconstruct the complete private key of one Asgard vault. That signing stack is off-chain Go code, and DefiLlama's registry records language null and targetType 'Chain' for this row (contrast the two 2021 THORChain rows, which it labels Solidity). Once the vault key was held, the Ethereum-side Router 0xd37bbe5744d730a1d98d8dc97c42f0ca46ad7146 simply honoured transferOut calls from the vault address as its source specifies; an onchain review of every Router transaction in blocks 25096819-25111182 (2026-05-15T00:00Z to 2026-05-17T00:00Z) shows only routine transferOut and depositWithExpiry traffic from Asgard vault accounts, with no anomalous entry point, no upgrade and no failed authorisation check. A cryptographic flaw in an off-chain MPC library is not a defect in executed EVM code, and two of the four affected chains (Bitcoin, and THORChain's own Cosmos-SDK L1) are not eip155 at all.

candidate.name: DAO Maker SHO deposit contract admin-role drain (August 2021)

disposition.reason: PRIVILEGED_ACTION: DAO Maker's own statement of 2021-08-12 says the company 'faced malicious use of one of our wallets with access to admin privileges', and the chain agrees. The sender 0x0eba461d9829c4e464a68d4857350476cfb6f559 had been operating DAO Maker admin functions since April 2021 (changeAssetDepositState on the SHO deposit contract 0x41b856701bb8c24cece2af10651bfafebb57cf49 on 2021-04-12 and 2021-04-21, addOrganizer/removeOrganizer/changeOrganizerAddress on 0x380c2c68ebcb38473e91b32e19ffb5519d7822b7 through 2021-08-03). At 2021-08-12T01:17:13Z it deployed the helper contract 0x1c93290202424902a5e708b95f4ba23a3f2f3cee (verified source, contract 'XXX', hardcoding victim 0x41b856..., collector 0xd8428836ed2a36bd67cd5b157b50813b30208f50 and USDC), then at 01:20:53Z and 01:27:39Z called grantRole(bytes32,address) on the victim to authorise it. The helper loops over user addresses calling selector 0x4b4f892a getUserAvailableBalance(address,address) and then 0x50b158e4 withdrawFromUser(address,address,uint256) - a role-gated administrative function that executed exactly as written for a caller holding the role. The first successful drain is 0x26aa86261c834e837f6be93b2d589724ed5ae644bc8f4b8af2207e6bd70828f9 at block 13007501 index 7, status 1 (an earlier attempt at 01:24:48Z, 0x11671333..., reverted before the second grantRole); about thirty further successful h(address[]) calls follow through 2021-08-12T18:18:02Z from 0xd8428836..., 0xed3112d1cf4895eb15f52e71f492235ed8ca7897, 0x414354db069cea6fa536c3d2ea1bbf5730b7715c and others. eth_getLogs over USDC and USDT for blocks 13006975-13008611 shows 0x41b856... emitting 5,252 outbound USDC transfers totalling 7,387,245 USDC in that window, matching DAO Maker's '5251 users affected, approximately 7m'. This is the August incident and is distinct from the already-admitted September 2021 record incidents/1/0xd5e2edd6089dcf5dca78c0ccbdf659acedab173a8ab3cb65720e35b640c0af7c.json (unprotected init() on the vesting minimal proxies). No deployed-code invariant failed here: an authorised administrative withdrawal path was used by whoever controlled the admin key.

candidate.name: Anyswap V3 router MPC key recovery from ECDSA nonce reuse

disposition.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the Anyswap V3 loss came from the attacker recovering the router's MPC private key, not from any contract flaw. Two transactions signed by the V3 MPC account reused the same ECDSA nonce (identical r value), which makes the secret key recoverable by elementary algebra; the signing stack is Anyswap's off-chain Go MPC node, and the router's Solidity simply honours calls from `mpc()`. The onchain response confirms the diagnosis: on the Ethereum AnyswapV4Router 0x6b7a87899490ece95443e979ca9485cbe7e71522 the MPC was rotated away from 0x8b44a687224496276811555efa3f2d0acd667a72 the day after the incident, in transaction 0x65651a6ba929fcb12ddcacd9a92fc131e1893dd0d0787f3c7cc787e4dad91ec6 (changeMPC(address), block 12806663, 2021-07-11T14:56:16Z, sent by the compromised MPC itself), with storage slot 0 (_oldMPC) becoming 0x8b44a687... and slot 1 (_newMPC) becoming 0x2a038e100f8b85df21e4d44121bdbfe0c288a869; nothing about the deployed code changed. This incident is distinct from the January 2022 AnyswapV4Router permit flaw already admitted as incidents/1/0xe50ed602bd916fc304d53c4fed236698b71691a95774ff0aeeb74b699c6227f7.json, which is a genuine code defect. Compromised credentials are excluded by METHODOLOGY, and a nonce-reuse bug in an off-chain signer is not executed EVM code.

KEY_COMPROMISE: Halborn's analysis and GAMEE's own disclosure attribute the loss to unauthorised access to an outdated GitLab repository that contained the project deployer's private key. Onchain, the compromised owner 0x566b788de3969d35711f6a0fc543b00ed7260cdc called the owner-only rescue function recoverERC721s (selector 0xc3666c36) on the verified PolygonGMEE token 0xcf32822ff397ef82425153a9dcb726e5ff61dca7 twice, at 2024-01-22T18:31:15Z (block 52629016, moving 299,999,999 GMEE to 0x16afa519642c932b073cd21d82162bdc7a471b86) and again at 20:31:03Z, then called transferOwnership on the same token at 22:35:32Z and on roughly fifteen further GAMEE contracts between 2024-01-23T03:10Z and 04:02Z. The PolygonGMEE source exposes recoverERC20s/recoverERC721s behind a _requireOwnership guard that executed exactly as written for the legitimate owner address, so no deployed-code invariant was violated; the defect is credential storage in an off-chain repository. Total press figure roughly 600m GMEE, about 7m USD.

CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION: rWBTC was listed without an RTokenConfig, leaving its underlying at the zero address, and transaction 0x9d2388a0c449c6265b968d86f0f54e75a5b82e2b04176e35eefdff5f135547ec then assigned the WBTC/USD feed to the zero-address key already used by native ETH. The reviewed incident anchors the resulting ETH price change, complete proxy history, seven-transaction campaign, and 1,233.956023308315527280 wstETH victim outflow.

NO_VICTIM_CONTRACT: the stolen SSX came out of externally owned wallets, and no token was minted. SOMESING Exchange (SSX) is a KIP-7/ERC-20 on Kaia (formerly Klaytn, eip155:8217) at 0xdcd62c57182e780e23d2313c4782709da85b9d6c, 18 decimals; eth_call totalSupply() returns exactly 5,054,571,320 SSX at the block for 2024-01-20T00:00Z, at latest, and at the block for 2024-02-03T00:00Z, so DefiLlama's 'Unbacked Mint' classification for this row is wrong (its 'Ethereum' chain and 'Solidity' language fields are wrong too - the SSG token 0x63dec0c0cf911d8967446ce422dd31f13e1e0556 that CoinGecko now lists did not yet exist on 2024-01-27, eth_getCode at Kaia block 144333904 returns 0x). Scanning every SSX Transfer log over Kaia blocks 144161104-144420304 (2024-01-25T00:00Z to 2024-01-28T00:00Z), plus a wider sweep of blocks 143642704-145025104 (2024-01-19 to 2024-02-04) that found no SSX transfer above 80,000,000 tokens other than the two below, shows the loss as two ordinary transfers out of funded EOAs: 162,047,818 SSX at 2024-01-26T16:18:02Z (block 144306186, tx 0x72e79da7d163c2b8ac55e0072f206dc073a11a488644f6e93276d4213c763544) from 0x3c2bcee93ad378e5f12fa4170d9d8a0707831d69 (balance 167,047,818 SSX immediately before) to 0x43edf0fdeaa30d3af23b0bb005d10833d8603ae4, and 210,446,564 SSX at 2024-01-26T20:18:21Z (block 144320605, tx 0xaaef0b8113d5ad48009a4df3ffb64b653007fb8547b09a9acae9b7850dac786e) from 0x0b7da3649ede697993c847c8169700bd911ebd57 to 0x1dc9223a74c088117772e769f9769911d4c95985, both followed within the hour by 3m-64m SSX tranches routed through 0x4c973076cc379af726d1cf4aaf0f952f77265bee into Kaia DEX pools. eth_getCode returns 0x for all four of those addresses, so every party in the causal path is an EOA and the only contract touched is the SSX token itself, which executed transfer() correctly. A wallet drain with no defective contract yields no code-age observation.

KEY_COMPROMISE: CertiK's post-mortem shows the proxy owner's key was used to transfer ownership (tx 0x733dd279b3d24f3415f3850b8eceafc651c1998163dcd0352b9e83c46e2b33d9) and then upgrade the proxy to code carrying burn and mint functions (tx 0xe4678ca53b308bb35f6fd393ca369e853f936788cd6c318cd38b0a25bec88b70), which do not exist in the audited code. The key holder burned about 60m PAID (tx 0x3a483dd881d98541ebbd51e9a64daa700546bae9c2b33a30c2192f9981334b9b), minted 59,471,745 PAID, and sold about 2.5m for roughly 2,040 ETH on Uniswap (tx 0x4bb10927ea7afc2336033574b74ebd6f73ef35ac0db1bb96229627c9d77555a0). The upgrade mechanism executed exactly as designed for the holder of the proxy key, so no deployed-code invariant was violated.

candidate.name: pNetwork pGALA proxy-admin key and white-hat drain

disposition.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE and PRIVILEGED_ACTION: SlowMist attributes the takeover to a leaked plaintext admin private key on GitHub, with the pGALA proxy admin owner replaced about 70 days before disclosure. The $4.3-4.6m figure is pNetwork's own privileged white-hat drain, 55.6b uncollateralised pGALA minted in two batches and sold for 12,977 BNB into the PancakeSwap pool (Beosin-traced tx 0x4b239b0a92b8375ca293e0fde9386cbe6bbeb2f04bc23e7c80147308b9515c2e), not an attacker's exploit of defective code, and no third-party theft from the bridge collateral is evidenced. A privileged mint-and-dump by the key holder is excluded either way.

candidate.name: Sweat Economy SWEAT NEAR token drain

disposition.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: the SWEAT token contract lives on NEAR Protocol and is written in Rust; the 13.71b SWEAT drain of foundation wallets executed inside NEAR's runtime and was routed through Ref Finance. NEAR has no eip155 chain id and no EVM bytecode whose age could be measured, and the exact contract defect was never publicly pinned beyond a token-contract flaw. Cohort conditions 1 and 2 both fail.

NON_EVM_CHAIN: the flaw is in Haveno's offchain trade-protocol messaging (a fake out-of-order arbitrator ACK overwrote the arbitrator address before multisig creation), and the 7,000 XMR moved inside Monero multisig wallets. Haveno clients are Java, the defect is message handling in peer software, and Monero has no eip155 chain id and no EVM contract state. There is no executed EVM code to age.

NON_EVM_CHAIN: eCurve and the PIZZA platform are EOS DAPPs written in C++; the infinite Tripool mint and collateral drain executed inside EOS contracts. EOS has no eip155 chain id and no EVM bytecode, so no code-age observation is possible.

KEY_COMPROMISE: attacker 0x2201037A1755eC48eC5F00Fea21A10A9E56f2Dd8 minted 99,000,000 TSR from the null address in tx 0x25093e573c116562c8839dc67a15ac21761271006a8dfe50b18fa475564bfcd1 at 2026-06-01T11:38:25Z after seizing ownership control of the contract, then dumped for about $2.4-2.5m USDT and bridged to Ethereum (1,285.5 ETH through Tornado Cash). The mint executed through the owner's mint authority as designed; no permissionless mint flaw in the deployed logic is evidenced. Re-enter only if a non-privileged mint path is verifiably pinned.

USER_ERROR, no code defect: LP owner 0xbe8351c14e5108a57a545dfa8669fa31aa6adc68 mistakenly transferred its Pancake V2 ATM/WBNB LP balance to the pair contract itself, and permissionless burn() redeemed the pair-held LP for the underlying 1,603.99 WBNB exactly as designed. No executable logic violated an invariant; the loss is a self-inflicted mis-transfer harvested by a watcher, not a vulnerability in executed code.

candidate.name: WEMIX Play Bridge Vault monitoring-key withdrawals

disposition.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the WEMIX Foundation attributes the 8.65m WEMIX drain across 13 successful of 15 withdrawals to stolen authentication keys for the NILE NFT platform monitoring system, uploaded to a shared repository and held by the attacker for two months before use. No smart-contract vulnerability is evidenced; the vault released funds to correctly authenticated withdrawal requests.

KEY_COMPROMISE: WEMIX discloses the attacker gained administrator privileges over the WEMIX$ contract and minted about 5,225,525 WEMIX$, swapping part into 30,736 WEMIX and 724,198.27 USDC.e before bridging out; about $724,000 was siphoned externally while the headline $6.25m counts the briefly circulating unauthorized issuance. The mint executed through the admin privilege as designed, with no evidenced defect in the deployed contract logic. candidate.name: THORChain ETH Router forged Deposit log (second 2021 incident)

disposition.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: the loss came from THORChain Bifrost accepting a forged log, not from a defect in the deployed router. Six returnVaultAssets calls in block 12878653 (indices 38,40,42,44,46,48) pass router=0x0 and asgard=attacker contract, so the empty coins loop runs and the unconditional asgard.call{value: msg.value} executes attacker code; that contract then emits the router Deposit topic0 0xef519b7e.. from its own address with topic1 = Asgard vault 0xf56cba49.., carrying each vaults full vaultAllowance read by staticcall in the same block. Bifrost matched logs by topic without checking the emitter and the real Asgard vault then signed legitimate transferOut payouts memoed REFUND:<returnVaultAssets txhash>. The routers own invariants held: vaultAllowance was never mis-decremented and no router asset moved except through the vaults authorised transferOut. THORChains post-mortem locates both bugs and both fixes in Bifrost, and the router runtime 0x8adfb73731c56be8d5d0300c3007489df1f935a40de483e803ef509935950b91 is identical at blocks 12796668, 12828215, 12833113, 12878652 and 13700000, so no redeployment followed. Noted for any future widening of the cohort: returnVaultAssets has no access control and makes an arbitrary external call, which is what let attacker code run inside a router-addressed transaction; that was judged a bypassed precondition rather than an invariant failure of the executed code.

Each matches a real Meter-side Deposit on Meter bridge 0x23894d2937a2a4a479f0407909da5b028049568e (e.g. nonce 3734 = 0xf209b1c1a4bc8b4618882c4cab5f37af912e57a17b1e599b62dd190099bedcae) in which the depositor actually transferred the MTRG into handler 0x139d9b458acda76457dd99db3a6a36ca9cb3bbf1. The MTRG itself was counterfeit: Meter block 100731418 (timestamp 1790198091 per rpc.meter.io, before the first BSC mint at 1790253525; miner 0xee2eeeed4ed8580669ed924abeb49f27f7d0bd65, the attacker) contains tx 0x63a588f79e16eef23e9cc43ccf8085cef05f346b8a327da5c6ff944170013c63 from 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 with r=s=0 crediting 1e31 wei MTR to the attacker, whose MTRG balance goes 0 -> 8e30 wei in that block. NON_EVM_CHAIN: the stolen asset was 4,502.9 BTC out of DMM Bitcoin's Bitcoin hot wallet (theft transaction 975ec405ac9dc9fa5ab8009d94d6a1fe31dff8a8127ea90d023104e52754e4d7, consolidation address 1B6rJRfjTXwEy36SCs5zofGMmdv2kdZw7P, then ten 500-BTC splits). Bitcoin is not an eip155 chain and no EVM contract held, released or accounted for the funds, so no executed EVM code exists to age. The joint FBI, DC3 and Japan NPA advisory of 2024-12-23 attributes the loss to DPRK TraderTraitor operators who social-engineered an employee of Ginco, DMM's wallet-management software vendor, with a fake pre-employment coding test, then used stolen session cookies to impersonate that employee inside Ginco's unencrypted communications system and alter a legitimate DMM withdrawal request in late May 2024. EVM chains appear only downstream, when proceeds were bridged through THORChain to Ethereum and Avalanche during laundering, which is not victim depletion.

candidate.name: HTX and HECO Bridge operator key compromise

disposition.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the HECO Bridge access control executed correctly and the attacker simply held the operator keys. The anchor transaction at block 18626540 index 6, status 1, is sent by 0x3d655889d197125fb90dcb72e4a287a8410ed1b9 with selector 0xd5b99d3c = withdrawNative(address,uint256,string,bytes32), whose source carries the onlyOperator and whenNotPaused modifiers and requires operatorRequireNum supporting operators. At block 18626539 getOperatorRequireNum() returns 2 and getAdminAddresses('operator') returns exactly [0x3d655889d197125fb90dcb72e4a287a8410ed1b9, 0x6b2286fc3a9265bab3f064808022aca54de4b6ce], so the attacker controlled both authorised operator keys and the 2-of-2 threshold was satisfied as written. The simultaneous HTX hot wallet drains from 0xb9f775179bcc7fcf4534700a48f09c590e390ead, whose eth_getCode is 0x, are ordinary EOA transfers with the same key-management origin. CertiK and SlowMist both conclude operator key compromise; no deployed-code invariant failed, so there is no code-age observation.

Both pre-recovery implementations are unverified bytecode. The anchor transaction at block 1339479 is sent by 0x6e8836f050a315611208a5cd7e228701563d09c5 with selector 0x7eee288d and status 1; the LockManager event carries 0x3b0033de4e2bd540000 = 17,413.96 ETH. BitForex never published a statement, so an operator key theft cannot be formally ruled out, but insider action and compromised credentials are both excluded by METHODOLOGY and neither yields a code-age observation.

DIRECT_PRIVILEGED_DRAIN: Infini's deployer retained DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE from contract creation. After 115 days the same authorized account granted itself the withdrawal role and immediately used role-gated calls to redeem and forward 49,516,662.977099 USDC. NON_EVM_CHAIN: Cashio was a Solana stablecoin protocol and the defective program is Rust running on the SVM, so it produces no eip155 code-age observation. The bug was a missing account-constraint chain in the mint instruction: the collateral bank account's `crate_collateral_tokens` was validated against the pool but the pool account itself was not validated against the crate, so an attacker could supply a fake Saber LP mint that chained back to attacker-controlled accounts and mint CASH against worthless collateral. Roughly two billion CASH were minted and drained for about 52.8m USD of UST/USDC LP collateral, and CASH depegged to zero. There is no EVM contract anywhere in the path - Cashio had no Ethereum, BSC or L2 deployment - so no victim contract, exploit transaction or executable code age can be recorded in this cohort. DefiLlama records the incident as Solana, 52.8m USD, missing input validation.

NON_EVM_CHAIN: Step Finance operates only on Solana and both attacker wallets and both theft transactions are Solana artifacts - collector LEP1uHXcWbFEPwQgkeFzdhW2ykgZY6e9Dz8Yro6SdNu and secondary 7raxiejD8hDUH1wyYWFDPrEuHiLUjJ4RiZi2z1u2udNh, the stake-authority/unstaking transaction 5EeXqPQci3ZnbFGWPJf622cLqLGnMuNcAr1rDGCizKRFt9owawCzovNpBC4xNh7A4a5p7Qkvsg8nPaYmw3MiYCvF and the 261,932 SOL withdrawal 4Ly35PsVTBNPVibpDRww6FC43pU5Tuw6UtaKECzcLKXtWTPyyvw1dw8LoNRLBDMgQUP81nN69mhiAEDJvzL8X317. No eip155 contract is in the path. The cause is also an exclusion ground on its own: an executive's device was compromised, most plausibly by social engineering, and the attacker used the resulting legitimate signing authority to reassign stake authorisation and approve withdrawals. No program was exploited and no on-chain invariant failed. DefiLlama records the incident as Solana, private key compromised, about 40m USD; rekt puts the realised figure at 27.3m USD.

candidate.name: Scream v3 aliased stablecoin price feeds

disposition.reason: CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION: Scream assigned scFUSD to Chainlink's USDC/USD aggregator at block 15846647, then set its collateral factor from zero to 0.85 at block 15846790. Both values persisted while fUSD traded below par. The first reviewed campaign borrow is 0x3fb9d16bc81ffca7f66a19fed0994dc4aaa9127d2f03e97dd5844524bd908b69: after supplying 461,109.4376 fUSD, the account borrowed 390,000 USDC against the aliased price. Three accounts' post-fUSD-supply Borrow amounts less every later RepayBorrow through block 123055284 leave an exact onchain lower bound of 24,480.522463 USDC, 2,875,037.153995981309124780 WFTM and 516.974432907347463696 WETH, valued at $2,106,269.47. This excludes the prearranged DEI exposure and all other affected accounts.

OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: the loss came from Crypto.com's own withdrawal system approving unauthorised requests, not from any contract. The onchain fingerprint is unambiguous: the collector 0x6e1218c55f1acb588fc5e55b721f1183d7d29d3d has code 0x and received 282 inbound value transfers from 282 distinct sender addresses totalling 4,836.25962449635 ETH, all inside two hours on 2022-01-17 between block 14024742 at 18:44:35Z (first transaction 0x49121cabf0b68f4755aa766090cbbc4fde4cca79d62365dadc4c92a83c683cda, 8.4207791732 ETH from 0x0c405c16c379b67d256f6883803e68d50dd2f327) and block 14025319 at 20:55:35Z. Many small transfers from many unrelated user accounts to one address is the signature of an exchange approving withdrawals it should not have, which is exactly what Crypto.com's own 2022-01-20 report describes: transactions were approved without the 2FA control being entered, affecting 483 accounts, 4,836.26 ETH, 443.93 BTC and about 66,200 USD in other currencies. DefiLlama files it as session key compromised. Nothing but correctly functioning transfers appears on chain, so there is no defective EVM code to age.

PRIVILEGED_ACTION and INSIDER_RUG: the code that failed was installed by the protocol's own proxy admin four minutes before it was used, so it never aged and was never trusted by anyone but its author. The two victim proxies are the BUSD vault 0x7e0c621ea9f7afd5b86a50b0942eaee68b04a61c and the WBNB vault 0x639f18c72b6a017bdd209c161d1617c9481a1e4d; reading the EIP-1967 slots at block 5381245 gives admin 0xc1f78cc844ac8e2dd9335e70b9c645e4d79130c5, the Meerkat deployer, and implementation 0x49509a31898452529a69a64156ab66167e755dfb, the honest logic that deployer created on 2021-03-03T16:28:07Z. The replacement implementations 0x9d3a4c3acee56dce2392fb75dd274a249aee7d57 and 0xb2603fc47331e3500eaf053bd7a971b57e613d36 were created by 0xfc76e716c35633a93ad621099a52ffda912fbedd at 2021-03-04T08:49:46Z and 08:49:58Z; the deployer key then called upgradeTo (selector 0x3659cfe6) on the WBNB vault at block 5381239, 08:53:10Z (0x063970f8625f250101a7da8abf914748cf8eaaaa9458041f1928501accfe5d6c) and on the BUSD vault at block 5381246, 08:53:31Z (0xf19fa4bcff4adaebeddd28c851458ba0f01ffedd52b62df56ace94e7c8842553). The new logic exposes an unprotected init(address) (0x19ab453c), called 24 seconds later at block 5381254 by 0x9542966f1114eaa5859201aa8d34358bfedbfa79 (0xfcf48681e382e9f9cc1d6a64ff30487306f6b869924c6594075fcc86b3b21f5d) to take ownership and drain. Balances confirm the outcome: the BUSD vault held 13,968,039.801181389726119981 BUSD at block 5381245 and 0 at block 5381300; the WBNB vault held 73,635.237472535387195192 WBNB at block 5381238 and 0 at 5381300. Meerkat first claimed a hack, and DefiLlama classifies it as a rugpull / admin drain. Attacker-authored code installed by the operator's own key yields no code-age observation.

candidate.name: Humanity Protocol foundation key and ProxyAdmin compromise

disposition.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE and PRIVILEGED_ACTION: the drain ran through an attacker-authored implementation installed by the legitimate ProxyAdmin, twelve seconds before use. The first leg is a plain ERC20 transfer of 6,045,060.xx H (token proxy 0xcf5104d094e3864cfcbda43b82e1cefd26a016eb) from the Humanity hot wallet 0x0fd9c51999ae46a0e1b21a235e0a529bbcc4612a to 0x9e995952ef7665b243eeef0693acd7fed7150504 at block 25274211, 2026-06-08T17:32:23Z (0x94a4b4a37439ad5c01a84b504c7f58eb5c2ab560352f147f78e62802bf4ee015). The bridge TransparentUpgradeableProxy 0x44f161ae29361e332dea039dfa2f404e0bc5b5cc, created 2025-06-20T18:56:35Z with implementation 0xfe1a06260b3b68f49862ae5d617686d78f454dea, then emits exactly one further Upgraded event, to 0xee1bd9356fe66591f600d5769f3e0e03f012cafa at block 25274909, 2026-06-08T19:52:11Z (0xca98624bf0425cba8fa89081be6981e34d7b3023f810350d0a0158de0eb4c551); the very next block carries 0xa665998ca9a2fcfe66d687647edede62c7acd554c7d35ea13c93788b8a129e5b, in which 0xd1ea823d421e0c829ee11f772af487fd352678ea calls execute(address) (0x4b64e492) on that fresh implementation to sweep the escrow. The H token proxy was likewise upgraded to 0xa4dcfaf7a2c0a533bc00a8a6d93b9f25f4583bb7 at 2026-06-09T01:05:11Z and restored to its original implementation 0x761c06a46d3c85ecd87cf6917b3de329b95829be on 2026-06-22. On BNB Chain the same proxy address 0x44f161ae29361e332dea039dfa2f404e0bc5b5cc was made to mint 100,000,000 H per call via mint(address,uint256) (for example 0x5a8f82f1064a7846ab3eb77bd1d36ec52dfd773c3957ad0aeea28da95fe9c5fb). The published account is that a director's laptop was infected through a spear-phishing email impersonating Bithumb, giving the attacker seven production keys backed up a year earlier and never rotated - three of six signers on the Ethereum Safe, three of five on the BSC Safe, and the ProxyAdmin on both chains, which had no timelock. DefiLlama records private key compromise, Ethereum and BSC, about 32m USD. Access control was satisfied throughout, so no executed code failed an invariant.

NON_EVM_CHAIN: the assets taken in Upbit's 2025-11-27 incident were Solana-ecosystem tokens held in a Solana hot wallet, so no eip155 contract is in the path and no EVM code age can be measured. DefiLlama's hacks dataset records the incident with chain ['Solana'] alone (36m USD, social engineering / malware), separate from Upbit's earlier 2019-11-27 Ethereum incident which the same dataset lists as ['Ethereum']. The cause is independently an exclusion ground: a custodial hot wallet's signing authority was abused, reported as malware / operator compromise rather than any contract flaw, and Upbit's own notice frames it as unauthorised outbound transfers that it covered from company assets. Distinguish this from the 2019 Upbit Ethereum theft; that is a different candidate and a different chain. This exclusion rests on the chain attribution plus the custodial cause; no victim contract or exploit transaction is named anywhere in the reporting because there is none.

KEY_COMPROMISE: Deribit's drained wallet is an externally owned account and the theft is a bare value transfer. eth_getCode is 0x for both the Deribit hot wallet 0x8d08aad4b2bac2bb761ac4781cf62468c9ec47b4 and the attacker 0xb0606f433496bf66338b8ad6b6d51fc4d84a44cd. The anchor is block 15878752 index 56, 2022-11-02T00:27:23Z, transaction 0xdd608c8c4e8d8529967955d89f9e71842e80c3c84d592c72054f68090a5a102c: 9,080.186758793618 ETH, empty calldata, from the hot wallet straight to the attacker, with a further 31.404516258391762 ETH at 08:35:23Z (0xf3a14bfddc65725b4a345e0bafa84afd328de1b9487339157a0f24c9085b66f2); Bitcoin legs ran in parallel to bc1qw5g8lw4kzltpdcraehy2dt6dqda8080xd6vhl4kg4wwsypwerg9s3x6pvk. Deribit's own statement of 2022-11-02 describes a hot wallet compromise covered from company reserves, with client funds unaffected and cold storage untouched; DefiLlama records a hot wallet key compromise of about 28m USD. Note that the 'DERIBIT' ERC20 that appears in the attacker's token history at 08:16:11Z the same morning is an unrelated spam token minted from the zero address, not part of the theft. No contract was called and no code failed.

candidate.name: GALA v2 dormant minter-role key compromise

disposition.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the anchor transaction is a bare mint(address,uint256) call (selector 0x40c10f19) sent at block 19913232 by externally owned account 0xec78b484a28a73f4f1cff23b9cd31aa12c1d9b4e directly to the GALA v2 token proxy 0xd1d2eb1b1e90b638588728b4130137d262c87cae; status 1, exactly one log, a Transfer from the zero address of raw 500000000100000000 (5,000,000,001 GALA at 8 decimals) to 0xe2ca471124b124831e231fb835778840ad100f97. That EOA was a dormant third party still holding the token's minter role after a 2023 partner integration; Gala's own incident report and rekt.news both describe a compromised minter key. The deployed code did exactly what it says: an authorised minter minted. There is no invariant failure in executed EVM code, so no code-age observation exists. The owner-controlled blocklist froze the recipient and capped realised loss at about 21.8m USD (5,913 ETH, returned two days later) against the roughly 216m USD nominal mint.
ATTACKER_DEPLOYED: the candidate victim was deployed by the attacker (0x7e7c1f0d567c0483f85e1d016718e44414cdbafe); attack infrastructure, not protocol code.

OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: SlowMist's incident alert states that BigONE's production network was breached and the operating logic of the account-management and risk-control servers was modified so that unauthorised withdrawals were signed and broadcast normally, and that no private keys were leaked. The named Ethereum sink is 0x9bf7a4ddca405929dba1fbb136f764f5892a8a7a; onchain it is an externally owned account (code size 0) whose earliest inbound transfers begin 2025-07-15T17:25:59Z and come from BigONE hot-wallet EOA 0xd4dcd2459bb78d7a645aa7e196857d421b10d93f (also code size 0): USDT 1,395,000 (tx 0x605e999e7be320c893...), INVI 4,702,000, XIN 20,730, CDT 1,901,300 and UNI 25,487 in the following minutes. The same actor holds BSC 0x9bf7a4ddca405929dba1fbb136f764f5892a8a7a, Solana HSr1FNv266zCnVtUdZhfYrhgWx1a4LNEpMPDymQzPg4R, Bitcoin bc1qwxm53zya6cuflxhcxy84t4c4wrmgrwqzd07jxm and Tron TKKGH8bwmEEvyp3QkzDCbK61EwCHXdo17c. Every EVM leg is a plain ERC-20 transfer between two EOAs: there is no victim contract and no defective executed code, only compromised offchain infrastructure.

OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: FixedFloat is a custodial instant-exchange service, not a protocol. About 26.1m USD of Bitcoin and Ethereum was taken from its own service wallets; FixedFloat confirmed the theft on 2024-02-18 and, as with its 2024-03-31 repeat, attributed the entry to vulnerabilities in third-party services it depended on rather than to anything it had deployed onchain. Both SlowMist Hacked and DefiLlama classify the event as third-party/infrastructure key leakage. The movement of funds is EOA-to-EOA on the Ethereum leg and UTXO spends on the Bitcoin leg; no smart contract of FixedFloat's was executed, so there is no victim contract to name and no executed EVM code whose age could be measured. I could not obtain a spot-checkable attacker address for this incident from any primary source, and the exclusion does not depend on one: a custodial service compromised through its own infrastructure is outside the cohort whatever the addresses are.

candidate.name: Kronos Research exchange API key compromise

disposition.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: Kronos Research is a proprietary trading firm. Its own disclosure (2023-11-19) reports unauthorised access to some of its centralised-exchange API keys; SlowMist Hacked records the event as an API-key attack and DefiLlama as 'API Key Compromised'. The roughly 25-26m USD loss was realised inside centralised-exchange accounts through attacker-issued orders and withdrawals, i.e. entirely offchain. No deployed contract was invoked and no protocol invariant failed, so there is no victim contract, no exploit transaction and no executable code whose age could be measured.

candidate.name: Resolv TheCounter compromised service key unbacked USR mint

disposition.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE and DIRECT_PRIVILEGED_MINT: TheCounter::completeSwap at block 24710031 accepted a 50,000,000 USR output amount from Resolv's long-lived trusted service EOA, then a second call minted 30,000,000 USR. Each call used the compromised service credential to mint directly; neither created persistent state for a later unprivileged exploit. The trace and complete Transfer-from-zero scan isolate these as the only abnormal mints in the window.

candidate.name: AFX USDC custody bridge validator hot-key compromise

disposition.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the victim is AFX's own USDC custody bridge on Arbitrum, verified source name 'Bridge', not a proxy, deployed 2026-05-08 by 0xa3eca683bcb9d38102033ca4609eb8f2c960847e; Arbitrum's native bridge was untouched. Decoding the anchor transaction's batchedCreateWithdrawals((address,address,uint64,uint64,(uint256,uint256,uint8)[])[],(uint64,address[],uint64[])) calldata at block 486657995 shows a single withdrawal of 24,150,000,000,000 (24,150,000 USDC at 6 decimals) to 0x2f2974fabc54dba33442261211c06bd20e0feefc, carrying five valid ECDSA signatures against the seven-member hot validator set 0x00bb84af06dac03bfe744da13df9d2d6fd8e77e5, 0x0c95ab7e26df9f63cc6e06df8ee897b822d8c77c, 0x27259f90d6ae500262ace6e8428434e0c1f308f5, 0x2e26de22a92e41704b3ea00cc65a6cda47b12c9e, 0x52d4d9ad78a53a69bd089ee8f282ce0cd0506da7, 0x5553ea7bda594ade7afe91d279779a42b2b84208 and 0xbb472bc3962ad02ac660429fdbb319b5bc66da7b with weights 1428/1429 each, so five stolen keys carried a real quorum. It was released three and a half minutes later by batchedFinalizeWithdrawals(bytes32[]) (tx 0x50d0b3ec6c3f5fce0f10abf81540bbb508f421494aa2b3480c4a264b0436547b, block 486658838, 2026-07-22T21:30:25Z), the same create-then-finalize cadence the bridge uses for ordinary traffic, and the proceeds were bridged to Ethereum by CCTP burns of 7,500,000, 5,895,000 and 5,000,000 USDC. Signature verification executed exactly as written against genuinely authorised keys, so this is validator key compromise and not a defect in the deployed bytecode.

KEY_COMPROMISE: Bitrue's own statement of 2023-04-14 reports 'a brief exploit in one of our hot wallets on 07:18 (UTC)' and about 23m USD withdrawn in ETH, QNT, GALA, SHIB, HOT and MATIC from a custodial wallet holding under 5 percent of exchange funds; SlowMist Hacked and DefiLlama both record it as a hot-wallet key compromise. A centralised exchange's custodial wallet is an externally owned account, so there is no victim contract and no protocol invariant to violate. I scanned Ethereum mainnet Transfer logs for QNT 0x4a220e6096b25eadb88358cb44068a3248254675, GALA 0x15d4c048f83bd7e37d49ea4c83a07267ec4203da and MATIC 0x7d1afa7b718fb893db30a3abc0cfc608aacfebb0 across blocks 17043816-17044112 (2023-04-14 06:59:59Z to 08:00Z) and found no bulk movement anywhere near the reported size, so the drained wallet was not an Ethereum mainnet address for those assets and no EVM exploit transaction can be named. The exclusion ground, custodial hot-wallet key compromise per the exchange's own disclosure, does not depend on pinning it.

KEY_COMPROMISE: the Swiss exchange Lykke lost about 22.4m USD, roughly 158 BTC and 2,161 ETH plus other assets, on 2024-06-04; the 2024-06-09 candidate date is the date the theft was publicised, not the date it happened. The published sinks are Bitcoin bc1qt64756h9aylujm9tpk826zndegpxtngmr6eqad and Ethereum 0x9172a72f5009ca609833819763a2722e53806443. Spot check: 0x9172a72f5009ca609833819763a2722e53806443 is an externally owned account (code size 0) and its earliest inbound transactions are plain ETH value transfers on 2024-06-04, 189.0165 ETH at 06:48:11Z from 0xc43d1cbacba9dda683a6286a95673c722c0fc488, 1,385.8617 ETH at 06:50:11Z from 0x054e993e0ecc5bf2797515adfc81d58cb8de0478, 300.0141 ETH at 08:05:23Z from 0x1bb2e2d4c782e0a0ea4341f20efdd93b730b1119 and 318.9896 ETH at 08:39:23Z, i.e. several Lykke custodial EOAs emptied in sequence. No contract was called, so no executed EVM code failed and there is no victim contract.

OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: SlowMist's analysis of the Indodax incident explicitly rules out a hot-wallet key compromise and concludes the exchange's withdrawal system itself was hacked, the attacker issuing round-number withdrawals (1 BTC, 3 BTC) with change returned to Indodax-controlled addresses; DefiLlama records the same event as infrastructure key leakage across Ethereum, Polygon and Optimism as well as Bitcoin, for 20-22m USD. Every leg is a custodial exchange wallet, an externally owned account acting on instructions from a compromised offchain withdrawal pipeline. No deployed contract executed defective code, so there is no victim contract and no code-age observation; the exclusion is on offchain infrastructure, which the cohort excludes regardless of chain.

NON_EVM_CHAIN and INSIDER_RUG: the IBXtrade presale ran on Solana, outside the eip155 cohort. The reported 21.8m USD is not an exploit loss at all but unreturned presale deposits: the sale targeted 2,000 SOL and raised over 160,000 SOL with a promise to refund the excess, after which the team ran a cap-raising poll on a site entirely under its own control, declared 65,000 SOL refunded and instead moved that SOL to addresses it had created, with participants reporting no refunds. SlowMist Hacked classifies it as a rug pull. Both grounds are independent: non-EVM chain, and insider action rather than a code defect, with no identifiable victim contract.

KEY_COMPROMISE: Bilaxy's own announcement (2021-08-29) says its ERC-20 hot wallet was hacked and about 295 tokens transferred to 0xa14d5da3c6bf2d9304fe6d4bc6942395b4de048b. Spot check confirms both ends are externally owned accounts with code size 0: 0xa14d5da3c6bf2d9304fe6d4bc6942395b4de048b receives its first token transfers at 2021-08-28T18:19:55Z, all from Bilaxy hot-wallet EOA 0xcce8d59affdd93be338fc77fa0a298c2cb65da59, beginning BIA 563,597,230 (tx 0x243d14ee07ff3578c0...), SPRK 1,570,398, COVA 1,497,243, RECOM 23,805, USDT 414,793, HOGE 1,183,626,188.5, CHAIN 455,867 and JDC 939,140 within the same minute, and continuing through hundreds of listings for the reported 21.7m USD. These are ordinary ERC-20 transfers signed with a stolen key: no contract of the exchange's was executed, so no victim contract and no measurable defective code exist. 2021-08-29 is the disclosure date, one day after the drain.

VICTIM_MISATTRIBUTED: the recorded victim is the UniswapV2 DAI/USDC pair, which contains no exploited flaw - it is only the CDP collateral token. The abused cdpAllow authority sits on a private, unverified, single-user CDP-management contract (0xbee1dee31365272bc6e5021c8ac66bede8bed641, deployed 2022-04-15, only ever called by its deployer), so there is no identifiable protocol victim contract (inclusion rule 2). Same attacker in both txs three days apart. Can re-enter only if a protocol-level victim is verifiably pinned.

candidate.name: SBI Crypto mining pool wallet drain

disposition.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: ZachXBT reported roughly 21m USD of suspicious outflows on 2025-09-24 from wallets belonging to SBI Group's mining subsidiary SBI Crypto, in BTC, ETH, LTC, DOGE and BCH, routed through five instant-exchange services and then into Tornado Cash, with suspected DPRK involvement; CoinDesk carried the report and SlowMist Hacked records it. Four of the five asset legs are on non-eip155 chains and every leg is a custodial mining-pool wallet, i.e. an externally owned account, so no deployed contract executed and no protocol invariant failed. I checked the only publicly labelled EVM address for the entity, Etherscan's 'SBI Crypto Pool' 0x8b4de256180cfec54c436a470af50f9ee2813dbb, and it has no transactions at all in blocks 23422005-23443482 (2025-09-23 to 2025-09-26), so that label is not the drained wallet and no EVM victim contract can be named.

NON_EVM_CHAIN and PRIVILEGED_ACTION: BONK and BonkDAO governance run on Solana, outside the eip155 cohort. The attacker bought roughly 4m USD of BONK to acquire sufficient voting power and passed proposal BIP-76, which transferred about 20m USD of BONK out of the treasury to wallets it controlled. SlowMist states explicitly that no smart contract was exploited and the DAO's own voting system was used as designed; DefiLlama classifies it as a governance attack via malicious proposal. Governance executing a proposal it validly approved is a privileged action, not an invariant failure of executed code, so neither ground admits it.

KEY_COMPROMISE: Lympo's statement to its community reports ten project hot wallets compromised and 165.2m LMT, about 18.7m USD, moved and dumped, crashing LMT 92 percent. Spot check on LMT 0x327673ae6b33bd3d90f0096870059994f30dc8af: externally owned account 0xe5e8229c057dcfa804195929293c88c708bd2bb4 (code size 0) received 6,250,000 LMT at 2022-01-10T11:21:09Z from 0x36d97147cf8e1b75254748cf0a102316fcc61697 and 148,600,820 LMT at 12:17:52Z from Lympo wallet 0x526232f70b97938e19394e57bc5ee1d5d929074e (tx 0x5b5e8c2f2c085879c92eb8af0b27f76d7369de04b16a183545e3e54f3e434b53), then sold 154,670,321 LMT into the 0x Protocol ExchangeProxy 0x74de5d4fcbf63e00296fd95d33236b9794016631 at 12:30:03Z (tx 0x4e476c490e5e6c0ce1de8bffeca0121b88a7bb28d272720a294fe2af124d1742). Every step is an ordinary ERC-20 transfer or swap signed with stolen keys; the LMT token and the router both behaved correctly, so there is no defect-bearing victim contract.

candidate.name: Rhea Finance NEAR leveraged trading slippage flaw

disposition.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: Rhea Finance (the merged Ref Finance / Burrow deployment) is a NEAR Protocol application; its lending market and leveraged-trading contracts are Rust/WASM contracts addressed by NEAR named accounts, not eip155 addresses, so the cohort's EVM-only condition excludes it whatever the mechanism. For the record the defect does look like genuine executed code rather than key compromise or configuration: Rhea's 2026-04-18 update attributes about 18.4m USD taken from the reserve pool to the attacker exploiting a vulnerability in the slippage-protection mechanism of the leveraged-trading path, after CertiK's first reading described fake token contracts seeded into new pools to mislead the oracle and validation layers; roughly 3.359m USDC and 1.564m NEAR were returned and 4.34m USDT frozen. Re-enter only if the cohort is ever widened beyond eip155.

candidate.name: Ostium OLP vault compromised oracle signer drain

disposition.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the victim is Ostium's public OLP liquidity vault on Arbitrum, TransparentUpgradeableProxy 0x20d419a8e12c45f88fda7c5760bb6923cee27f98 over implementation 0xacff332d0d8c34162be6bbabf7d676fea7cd0f3e (verified name OstiumVault). Scanning native USDC 0xaf88d065e77c8cc2239327c5edb3a432268e5831 Transfer logs across blocks 484136200-484138604 shows the vault paying attacker 0x321df194646029e7a6193ea05573d4b9c398bfd9 in six settlements: 6,290,901.90 + 4,763,111.22 + 718,959.42 USDC in the anchor transaction at block 484137113 (2026-07-15T14:18:48Z), then 4,493,501.10 (0xd9f91cc3eaec695f45bffad3a068fa52e1625ed44bfcc47d6ac3938f78d9061d), 3,594,800.70 (0x3b04639ab9b40760b2138e7bfa7eccc9657f3a767a5c414dbb1b3632ed71f3bf), 2,696,100.30 (0x6c254483fa47a14622662e792bc3728ab3c408a33d3cbb5712434ba96f5ecdc2) and 1,078,439.58 (0xfaf6d3d4d7f1a75bfc11fb4d36d0525791546267fda1cdd371703ce03ae8ba8c), about 23.6m USDC in total, all batched through attacker contract 0xfe12f6360000de49d5506d52ee5ac4bc9dd5bd2e from EOA 0xd1794196f0fc99c7f27970e661597d77d9a85869. The window matches founder Kaledora Fontana's statement that funds left the public OLP vault between 14:18 and 14:23 UTC. SlowMist and DefiLlama both attribute the exploit to a compromised oracle signer key used to submit fraudulent future-dated price reports, which the settlement path then honoured; without that key the attacker's trades do not settle profitably, so the stolen signer is the necessary cause. Reviewer flag: if a full post-mortem later shows the vault would also have accepted stale or future-dated reports from an honest signer, the acceptance logic becomes an independent code defect and this lead should be reopened.

KEY_COMPROMISE: Grinex, the Kyrgyzstan-registered exchange that absorbed the sanctioned Garantex's liquidity and users, suspended trading and withdrawals after a hot-wallet infrastructure breach. Elliptic puts the theft at about 15m USD of USDT taken from Grinex-associated wallets and routed through TRON and Ethereum, then converted into TRX and ETH to reduce the chance of a Tether freeze; the exchange's own notice claims over 1bn rubles, about 13.1m USD. TRON is not an eip155 chain, and the Ethereum leg consists of ERC-20 transfers out of custodial externally owned accounts, so no deployed contract executed defective code and there is no victim contract to name.

KEY_COMPROMISE: about 14.8m USD was taken from the custodial wallets of Rain, the Bahrain-licensed exchange, across Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and Solana on 2024-04-29; DefiLlama classifies the event as a private-key compromise and the public reporting attributes it to DPRK-linked actors, with no protocol or contract exploit alleged by any source. Three of the four asset legs are on non-eip155 chains and all four are exchange custody addresses, i.e. externally owned accounts moved with stolen keys, so there is no victim contract, no exploit transaction against deployed code and nothing whose code age could be measured. SlowMist Hacked carries no entry for this incident and I could not obtain a spot-checkable address for any leg; the exclusion ground does not depend on one.

INSIDER_RUG: the deployed Staking contract carries a hardcoded backdoor beneficiary, so no invariant of the code failed and there is nothing to age. The seed row's summary that transferOwnership had no access control is wrong - transferOwnership is onlyOwner, but the deployed Ownable._checkOwner() reads: if (owner() != _msgSender() && _msgSender() != 0xe746c9043aa0106853c5e4380a9a307fe385378e) revert, with that address literal compiled into the runtime (one occurrence in the 24,462-byte runtime at block 97836947). Proved by simulation at block 97836947, where owner() is 0x..dEaD: transferOwnership succeeds from 0xe746c904.. and reverts both from project operator 0x1df1d1e2.. and from an unrelated address. The same literal appears in sibling contracts IConf 0x08f7fd1b.. and PotatoCoin 0x84791ba6.., all deployed in one batch on 2026-01-29 funded by operator 0x1df1d1e2.., and the backdoor EOA was funded 41 days before the victim contract existed (block 72147100). Exploiting it requires being that specific address, so this is author-installed authority rather than a defect any caller could trigger. The PoC asserts 346,137.034345014454603094 USDT, but the incident yields no code-age observation.

candidate.name: WOO X exchange developer-environment phishing drain

disposition.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE and KEY_COMPROMISE: DefiLlama's hack registry (api.llama.fi/hacks) records this as classification 'Social Engineering', technique 'Phishing', targetType 'CEX', 14.0m USD, spread across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Arbitrum and BSC. The compromised asset was WOO X's own developer environment; the attacker then signed ordinary withdrawals out of exchange-custody wallets. One of the four asset legs (Bitcoin) is not an eip155 chain, and on the EVM legs an exchange hot wallet is an externally owned account: no contract of WOO X's executed, no protocol invariant was violated, and there is no deployed code whose age could be measured. WOO X published no contract address or exploit transaction and I could not obtain a spot-checkable custody address for any leg; the exclusion ground does not depend on one, because a phished developer credential is outside the cohort whichever address was drained.

KEY_COMPROMISE: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Hot Wallet Key Compromised', targetType 'CEX', 13.7m USD taken from the Abu Dhabi exchange M2 across Ethereum, Solana and Bitcoin. Two of the three legs (Solana, Bitcoin) are outside eip155, and the Ethereum leg is ERC-20 and ether transfers signed out of custodial externally owned accounts. M2 operates no deployed protocol contract on any chain, so there is no victim contract, no exploit transaction against deployed code, and no code state whose age could be measured. M2 covered the loss from its own reserves the same week; that does not create a contract-level defect.

VICTIM_MISATTRIBUTED: the recorded victim is the UniswapV2 DAI/USDC pair, which contains no exploited flaw - it is only the CDP collateral token. The abused cdpAllow authority sits on a private, unverified, single-user CDP-management contract (0xbee1dee31365272bc6e5021c8ac66bede8bed641, deployed 2022-04-15, only ever called by its deployer), so there is no identifiable protocol victim contract (inclusion rule 2). Same attacker in both txs three days apart. Can re-enter only if a protocol-level victim is verifiably pinned.

NON_EVM_CHAIN: DefiLlama places the incident on EOS and records the defective code's language as C++. EOSIO contracts are C++ compiled to WASM and are addressed by 12-character account names, not by eip155 addresses, so there is no address, no runtime bytecode and no codeHash the verifier could resolve. The mechanism itself does look like a genuine executed-code defect rather than a key compromise: flash.sx was an EOSIO flash-loan primitive and vaults.sx the yield vault backing it, and the attacker re-entered the vault from inside the flash-loan callback for about 13m USD. The cohort is eip155-only, so it is excluded on chain grounds regardless. Re-enter only if the cohort is ever widened beyond eip155.

KEY_COMPROMISE: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Hot Wallet Key Compromised', targetType 'CEX', 13.9m USD, with no chain attribution at all because the drained assets were custodial balances rather than protocol positions: about 61 BTC, 350.5 ETH, 10,000,000 WEMIX and 220,000 USDT, roughly a quarter of the Korean exchange GDAC's total custody. The BTC leg is not an eip155 chain and the remaining legs are ordinary transfers signed out of exchange-owned externally owned accounts, so no deployed contract of GDAC's executed and no invariant of any contract was violated. Dates differ across sources: DefiLlama records 2023-04-08, the incident occurred on 2023-04-09 KST, and the web lead's 2023-04-10 is the public announcement.

OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: the loss was 277 BTC, about 12.7m USD, released from pNetwork's Bitcoin-side vault. DefiLlama records the event as 'Bridge & Cross-Chain' / 'Spoofed Event Log' over chains BSC and Bitcoin, and names the defective code's language as Rust: the pTokens bridge core that decides whether a redeem happened is Rust software running off-chain, not EVM bytecode. I verified onchain that the BSC side lost nothing. The pBTC token 0xed28a457a5a76596ac48d87c0f577020f6ea1c4c (AdminUpgradeabilityProxy over implementation 0xd61372d1c3e0a0925467317425359fb2959fe186) has zero Transfer events from the zero address in blocks 11035530 (2021-09-18T23:59:58Z) through 11092771 (2021-09-21), i.e. no unbacked mint, and the largest single pBTC movement in that whole window is 51.7499 pBTC at block 11067993 (tx 0x2876012ade42384bd6a5abe3326f4fa1c02b13c7121e8333b49216b8d9e3e88e), nowhere near 277. So there is no EVM victim contract: the depleted asset is native BTC on a non-eip155 chain and the failure is an off-chain validator honouring a log it did not authenticate, the same shape as the already-excluded THORChain Bifrost incidents.

candidate.name: Ionic Protocol fake LBTC collateral listing

disposition.reason: OFFCHAIN_SOCIAL_ENGINEERING and ATTACKER_INTRODUCED_ASSET: Ionic's postmortem says the exploiter impersonated Lombard through weeks of business-development talks, supplied a market and oracle for an imitation LBTC, and induced Ionic to approve it as collateral; it identifies no contract or authorization bypass. Onchain, the imitation LBTC proxy 0x964dd444e3192f636322229080a576077b06fba3 was created in 0x9b90a303f8f40f5c9157ecb17c439841eb46885eec98589c485762cf0836051f at Mode block 18135008 on 2025-01-09. Ionic's Safe 0x8fba84867ba458e7c6e2c024d2de3d0b5c3ea1c2 then deliberately routed that exact token to oracle 0x04ffa53a90a8ded9ae83f64596c5783397c1cfb0 in 0xf0d10fcdb3c385bda3d3df040b2c0c7cb68d5babbd1e89bb41910581d1206a0d, created and listed ionLBTC 0xade794534c05f79981337e73dc2a987cdff1958d with that token as underlying in 0x0b867a1dfd937981202cef46d533bbf66b4f737ba38a37d7fc633647e96d4e6d, set its 250-LBTC supply cap in 0x147d6c137e52f88b0ced1fb2b11d752be9f2598b136869f8a54fc9add56030f7, and set its 50 percent collateral factor in 0x4204bddeba37cc0674f552247fa68904faae2d947b12a7d57de47f291681abaa. All four Safe transactions succeeded. The attacker later minted the imitation token in 0x9aa3fd43a6b0f85b4f1bf74f0c9e79773f238591d9c6fe666287bd2c8ac19009 and supplied it through ordinary ionLBTC mint calls beginning with the candidate transaction. The listing is the victim's execution of an attacker-authored social-engineering plan, not a latent code or causal authorization defect whose age predicts battle-tested security; assigning age from the listing would age attack machinery and offchain due diligence.

KEY_COMPROMISE: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Hot Wallet Key Compromised', targetType 'Payments', 9.7m USD (the web lead's 11.8m is the higher press figure), across Ethereum, Tron and Arbitrum. Triple-A is a licensed payment processor holding client crypto in company custody; the drained balances are custodial externally owned accounts, and the Tron leg is not an eip155 chain. No Triple-A protocol contract exists to be the victim, no deployed code was executed outside its specification, and no code state can be aged. The company's own disclosure attributes the loss to unauthorised access to company wallets, not to any contract.

KEY_COMPROMISE and OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'Key Leaked via Infrastructure', targetType 'CEX', 11.5m USD, across Ethereum, Tron, Solana and Polygon. The Taiwanese exchange BitoPro's own disclosure and the subsequent DPRK attribution describe malware planted during a hot-wallet system migration that exfiltrated signing material from the exchange's own servers; the outbound movements are then ordinary transfers from custodial externally owned accounts. Two of the four legs (Tron, Solana) are outside eip155 and none of the four involves a BitoPro-deployed contract, so there is no victim contract and no defective executed code to age.

candidate.name: UXLINK Safe owner takeover and unauthorised mint

disposition.reason: SIGNING_PLANE_COMPROMISE and ATTACKER_INTRODUCED_CONFIGURATION: Safe transaction 0xed932cf2d55dce38ac9d16a7bbeae1d7ba74895e05d6933493f3a0d800637e9b at Arbitrum block 381858847 was confirmed by two existing EOA owners, 0x423f62a367088236c2b330f1bc0b082ce499c421 and 0x69522621e79eff14b0a58a8ffaef98dfba388767. It successfully called addOwnerWithThreshold(0x2ef43c1d0c88c071d242b6c2d0430e1751607b87,1) on the Safe; AddedOwner, ChangedThreshold(1), and ExecutionSuccess all confirm that the required authorization held. Four seconds later the new owner alone executed 0x371ca7462cbcbb5d7a40a9390b82f3cba0c01694270b1db18e291302c438ccae, removing all three prior owners. The following day the one-owner Safe made six successful ordinary mint(address,uint256) calls to UXLINK token 0x1a6b3a62391eccaaa992ade44cd4afe6bec8cff1. Whether the original signatures were obtained by social engineering or stolen keys, no Safe or token authorization check failed. The owner replacement was the attack itself and the resulting state was attacker-controlled attack machinery, not a latent victim-code or causal-configuration vulnerability to age.

KEY_COMPROMISE and OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'Key Leaked via Infrastructure', 11.4m USD, across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base and Solana. Garden is an intent-based cross-chain swap protocol whose solvers hold their own inventory and sign fills; the compromise was of a solver's operational infrastructure, so the attacker moved solver-owned capital with a stolen key rather than defeating any invariant of Garden's HTLC contracts. The Solana leg is outside eip155. This is a different event from the 2026-07-26 Garden database breach (450k USD), which DefiLlama lists separately. No Garden contract was drained by an attacker without the solver's key, so there is no defect-bearing victim contract; if a later postmortem shows the settlement contracts released escrowed user funds on a signature they should have rejected, the lead should be reopened.

NON_EVM_CHAIN: DefiLlama records Blend Pools V2 on Stellar, 10.97m USD, classification 'Oracle Manipulation', technique 'Spot Price Manipulation'. Blend is a Soroban lending protocol; its pools are Rust/WASM contracts addressed by Stellar strkeys (C... contract IDs), not eip155 addresses, so no address, runtime bytecode or codeHash exists that this dataset could measure. The cohort is eip155-only, so the incident is excluded on chain grounds whatever the mechanism. Re-enter only if the cohort is ever widened beyond eip155.

KEY_COMPROMISE and PRIVILEGED_ACTION: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Deployer Key Compromised', 10m USD across Ethereum, BSC and Cronos. Verified onchain: the only mint of the DEGO token 0x88ef27e69108b2633f8e1c184cc37940a075cc02 in blocks 14174988-14187946 (2022-02-10 to 2022-02-11) is 953,590.33 DEGO to 0xd2b2755a4bdcaf415e9a74e3efe41d23d2f70c53 at 2022-02-10T00:56:12Z, block 14175251, in tx 0x4195bf8ad88ee40a3df2d851820d4d35a8bde498a2b369040f71aaf1c1b23251. That transaction is a direct call of mint(address,uint256) (selector 0x40c10f19, 138-byte calldata) from externally owned account 0x20fe4b1ed95911487499e53355bb8f14a881d735 straight to the token, with no intermediate contract and no defeated check: the caller simply held the token's minter authority. The BSC-side DEGO 0x3fda9383a84c05ec8f7630fe10adf1fd13c5c79b has zero mints in the corresponding window (blocks 15118825-15176352). A privileged mint executed by whoever holds the minter key is the correct behaviour of the deployed code, so there is no invariant failure to age.

sources.ref: onchain review (no exploit tx in this row; DeFiHackLabs src/test/2024-01/MIMSpell2_exp.sol names the same victim. Incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> ethereum block 19119184, 2024-01-30T12:00:00Z). The victim 0x7259e152103756e1616A77Ae982353c3751A6a90 is an EIP-1167 minimal proxy created at block 16520538, 2023-01-30T15:28:47Z; its 45-byte runtime (0x363d3d373d3d3d363d73c4113ae18e0d3213c6a06947a2ffc70ad3517c775af43d82803e903d91602b57fd5bf3) hardcodes the CauldronV4 master 0xc4113ae18e0d3213c6a06947a2ffc70ad3517c77 in the bytecode rather than in storage, so the delegate target cannot be repointed. The clone runtime is byte-identical at its creation block and the incident block, and the master (created 2023-01-26T02:59:11Z, block 16488159) itself contains zero DELEGATECALL opcodes and emits no EIP-1967 Upgraded event. The effective code therefore never changed after the clone was deployed and the deployment basis is exact.

re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis (re-check of the existing note). The clone's 45-byte runtime and the CauldronV4 master 0xc4113ae18e0d3213c6a06947a2ffc70ad3517c77's 22 kB runtime are each byte-identical at 13 sample points across [16520538, 19119184], so neither the hardcoded delegate target nor the master's code moved before the incident.
exploit tx backfilled and verified onchain (block 19118660): a contract-creation tx deploying and running the exploit, CauldronV4 victim in receipt logs, matching the DeFiHackLabs MIMSpell2 PoC

candidate.name: Pricer ownership manager unrestricted transferOwnership
candidate.notes: The pricer-ownership manager deployed with the December oracle upgrade exposed transferOwnership(address,address) with no caller restriction, so the attacker took ownership of the stETH/AAVE/LINK/WBTC pricer proxies, swapped in a malicious pricer implementation, wrote arbitrary expiry prices into the Opyn Oracle and redeemed worthless oTokens against the MarginPool.

sources.ref: callTracer review of the takeover tx: attacker helper 0x1a7efc51... calls 0x9d7b3586... with selector 0x6d435421 (transferOwnership(address,address)), which forwards f2fde38b to pricer proxy 0xa4aC089B972206021EceB50a494d60B1c74E534e, then setImplementation (0xd784d426) to malicious pricer 0xE1f09d50F733993b11bF3054bD870d688401984c and pushes an expiry price into Oracle 0xb5711dAeC960c9487d95bA327c570a7cCE4982c0; the same pattern repeats for 0xb78E96750497e319Bb6a09a8Dc7C75fE32937AdA. Victim creator 0xb594f7e7ad548f63db49665ae4e3d3f8457cf6f5 is not the attacker; the MarginPool drain followed 10 blocks later in tx 0x16eded2553e0793472a6283093738152de1dd0e2504836856fbcaf88cc4a2687 Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim's fallback is a non-standard proxy path that DELEGATECALLs whatever address sits in plain storage slot 1 (no EIP-1967 or beacon slot is used); slot 1 reads 0x0 at the incident block 23995254, so that path dead-ends in STOP and every executed instruction comes from the victim's own runtime, which is byte-identical at the creation block 23979057 and the incident block 23995254. The only other DELEGATECALL is an OpenZeppelin Address helper on a target passed in by the caller. Deployment is therefore the right basis, and the flawed transferOwnership(address,address) is code the deployer shipped 2.3 days earlier, not something the attacker installed.

disposition.reason: An admitted incident declares this discovery lead.

sources.ref: re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis. The victim is an Aave-fork InitializableImmutableAdminUpgradeabilityProxy: its EIP-1967 implementation slot held 0x2d5bc0f897ad211ef9f954eadf59c43fb1ec4788 continuously over a 25-point probe of [15927425, 21120284] and that implementation's runtime is likewise constant. callTracer on the exploit tx shows three further delegatecall targets from the pool's context: 0x10ea06d74f8d7681f584558d9200cc7a9b852a9f and 0xf25d23913c6c8de1c3c25539fdabee1e51a06c63 are link-time libraries (runtime begins 73<self>3014) with constant code, and 0x85b79018c781b499f2878bee14e4e8b5db31ac61 is the LendingPoolCollateralManager, which is NOT hardcoded - it is resolved through the addresses provider 0xA91B9095eFa6C0568467562032202108e49c9Ef8. Binary-searching eth_call of getLendingPoolCollateralManager() over the same range shows it set once, at block 15927451 (2021-05-07T09:18:35Z, 135 s after the proxy's creation) and never changed before the incident, so the deployment basis stands.

disposition.reason: An admitted primary incident anchors this row's exploit transaction.

candidate.name: bZx Fulcrum ETHDenver flash-loan margin trade
candidate.notes: iTokens_loanOpeningFunctions.takeOrderFromiToken guarded the collateral check with a short-circuiting OR - require((loanDataBytes.length == 0 && sentAmounts[6] == sentAmounts[1]) || !OracleInterface(oracle).shouldLiquidate(...)) - so with empty loanDataBytes the left operand was true and shouldLiquidate() was never called, letting a 5x short open against the iETH pool that was instantly underwater after 5,637 ETH was swapped into 51 WBTC on Uniswap V1.

sources.ref: onchain review: the exploit path is attacker contract 0x4f4e0f2cb72e718fc0433222768c57e823162152 -> iETH LoanToken 0x77f973fcaf871459aa58cd81881ce453759281bc (marginTradeFromDeposit, selector 0x1c5d1da5) -> BZxProxy 0x1cf226e9413addaf22412a2e182f9c0de44af002 (takeOrderFromiToken, selector 0xb1eac3ad), which DELEGATECALLs the iTokens_loanOpeningFunctions module 0xf0a42ec4ebb7664af5dae5c3209345d545da838a carrying the skipped shouldLiquidate check. BZxProxy was created 2019-01-28 by 0xadff3ada12ed0f8a87e31e5a04dfd2ee054e1118 (bZx deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0x148426fdc4c8a51b96b4bed827907b5fa6491ad0. BZxProxy is a per-selector module registry (mapping(bytes4 => address) targets) that emits no EIP-1967 Upgraded event, so module installs were recovered by calling targets(bytes4) under binary search over block height: targets(0xb1eac3ad) first held 0xfbc580e4f16234d5783314f1d4195971eff453f4 and was rewritten to 0xf0a42ec4 at block 9443140 (2020-02-08T16:24:12Z, tx 0x7e49e3da0817322d9a118957fd535e10ae9e19e0022181d227f01e9b7c6d3d5f from the bZx deployer via settings contract 0xbb536eb24fb89b544d4bd9e9f1f34d9fd902bb96); the other selectors the exploit drives were installed earlier (targets(0x327ab639) 2019-08-08, targets(0xb1fd9e05) 2019-12-06), so the flawed module is also the most recent install and sets the age at 6.39d rather than the 3.16y deployment figure. bZx replaced this module three days later - the same selector resolves to 0x3756fa458880fa8fe53604101cf31c542ef22f6f in the 2020-02-18 transaction.
